status: authored 2026-09-29; file-valid only. Nothing here has been seen in a running game.
supersedes_why: the COBBLEVERSE donor shell (23x27, one oval room, no second storey) is taken down by tools/gym_demolish.py and this hall is built on its lot. docs/world-building/GYM_BUILDINGS_BRIEF.md: the owner rejected a shaft into a cave under the shell and asked for a large building with the puzzle inside it. The works under this gym - the throat, the galleries, the geyser - are filled in by the same demolition.
name: The Assay House
reading: Blaine's town is a research town on the crater rim that studies the cone's energy and keeps the mound between itself and the fire (docs/world-building/TOWN_CHARACTER.md: core-sample racks, a field laboratory, survey tables, a fumarole vent; blackstone, basalt, tuff, terracotta, acacia and copper instruments). Its plan puts the gym alone at the end of a bare basalt causeway, east of the square, on the open rim: 'You leave the town to get there.' So the gym is the one building the town will not put next to its houses - the house over the vent itself. Inside, a nine-block blackstone flue stands in the middle of the floor from the pad to the roof, and the whole hall is the scaffolding the researchers have hung around it to read it: the drill floor, the assay deck five up, the gauge gallery thirteen up, and the crown on the flue's head where four sampling hoods open into it. Three hoods are dry and stop on packed straw; the fourth is the cooled throat, with light and water thirteen below. You go down it on purpose, and Blaine is in the assay vault at its foot, which has no other door.
reading_why_vertical: the rejected interior for this site was right about one thing and the independent audit said so: the drop into a lit throat was the route finding it passed. What was rejected was burying it. GYM_BUILDINGS_BRIEF.md's own line - 'a vertical instrument hall, above ground, is open to you' - is taken literally: the throat is now the flue of a building that stands on the rim, and every stage of it is inside the hall where it can be seen from the door. Blaine's verb stays the leap; nothing else in the six gyms asks a player to step off something on purpose.

site.lot_source: data/placements.json settlements.gym7_town.plan.anchors gym7_gym (rect, level 106, facing west). The prep cuts and fills the lot to that level (tools/place_town.py: 'a levelled lot is cut and filled to its level by the prep, so that is its ground'), and the plan's prep note records the flat: 'The square and the road sit on the flat at y106-108 ... The causeway is level across the rim.'

ground.why: the pad is the ground here, and the raw heightmap agrees with it: GYM_BUILDINGS_BRIEF.md's corrected envelope table measures the raw ground under this lot as y106 flat, and the lot's declared level is 106. Neither number was read from a world; nothing in this record steps down a slope, so no column needs tools/ground.py.

site.footprint_size_why: 23 by 23, square, in a 33 x 31 lot: margins 5 west, 5 east, 4 north, 4 south to the lot edge, and the roof's one-block eaves and the forecourt apron still leave 2 west, 4 east, 3 north and 3 south. Square because the building is a house built round a flue and has no long axis; the donor shell it replaces was 23x27.
site.facing_why: the lot anchor is `facing: west` and the causeway (data/placements.json streets, `causeway`, [6088,4995] to [6152,4995], three wide) runs straight at the hall's west door, which is centred on z4995.
site.height_why: twenty above the floor, ridge y126. The town's own landmark is the instrument mast on the mound at (6015,4935), top y128 (docs/world-building/TOWN_CHARACTER.md); this hall's ridge stays under it, so the mast is still the thing you see over the town and the gym is the thing at the end of the causeway.

bounds_why: the hall (6159..6181 x 4984..5006), its one-block eaves (x6158 and x6182, z4983 and z5007), the forecourt apron where the causeway ends (x6156..6158) and the quench basin's footing three courses under the floor (y103..y106 under the flue only). leader.name: Blaine
leader.why: EXP-013 E2 (VERIFIED, on staging): a bare rctmod:trainer_spawner set by command with TrainerIds on a redstone block spawned the leader and he battled. The donor template does the same thing. Taking the shell down removes the template's own spawner at [6169,106,4988], so this one is the only kanto_blaine in the town and the badge cannot be won without reaching the assay vault (a persistent leader spawner anywhere awards the badge: verified on staging 2026-09-24, docs/STATE.md).

rooms.why: the causeway's end: bare basalt apron, two lamp posts, and the hall's door. Nothing else is built on the rim, as the town plan says.

the working floor round the flue's foot: the assay furnace, the sample barrels, the core racks, and the packed straw the cores are crated in. From the door the whole climb is legible - the spoil steps on the left, the deck over them, the broken flight to the right, the gantry stair on the far side and the gallery above it.
the assay deck along the north wall, six above the floor, on acacia posts. Stage 1 ends here and stage 2 leaves from its east end.
the flue: nine by nine of blackstone from the pad to the roof space, solid apart from what is cut in it. It is the building's reason and its puzzle.

the gauge gallery at thirteen above the floor: a walk corbelled off the flue's east face at its north end, the gantry stair's landing beyond that, and southward the assay vault's roof at the same level with the geyser's mouth in it. The only opening into the crown is off it.
the flue's head, seven by seven, parapet to y122 and the roof over it. Four sampling hoods open in its floor, one at each corner, all four rimmed the same.
three blind hoods, two by two, stopping six down on packed straw with a ladder back up; and the cooled throat, which does not stop.
the cooled throat: two by two, nine blocks of dark, opening into the basin chamber.
the quench basin at the flue's foot: three courses of water whose surface is the hall's own floor level, under a basalt ceiling, lit by four lanterns whose light is what shows up the cooled throat.

the assay vault: where the cores are read, and where Blaine is. Five by ten and twelve high, sealed on all six sides; its only door is the passage from the basin, and its only way out is the tapped geyser in its east corner.

route.why: five courses of tuff spoil stepped against the west wall - tops y107, 108, 109, 110, 111 at z4995 down to z4991 - onto the assay deck, whose planks are at y112.
route.not_skippable: the deck stands six above the floor and its posts are under its own planks, where nobody can stand on them. The three core racks on the floor top at y110, two below the deck's walking level, and no player mounts two blocks. The broken flight on the south side climbs higher and reaches nothing.

route.why: the dismantled scaffold: six steps north along the south wall to y112, then four west to y116. It is the taller of the two climbs from the floor and it is the wrong one.
route.not_skippable: its head stands one block from the flue's south face, which is sheer from the floor to the parapet coping at y122, five above it; the crown's parapet is pierced on the east side only. Stepping off it is a ten-block fall onto the straw of the crating floor, which costs nothing.

route.why: off the deck's east end, seven acacia treads rising one course each from y113 at z4985 to y118 at z4990, then the stair tower's head at y119 over z4991-4992, which is the gallery's level.
route.not_skippable: the treads start on the deck, six above the floor, and the tower below them is sheer for thirteen courses. The gallery is thirteen above the floor and nothing else on the drill floor or the deck comes within three of it.

route.why: west along the landing bridge and onto the gauge gallery, two wide, hung off the flue's east face; the opening through the parapet at x6174, z4994-4996 is the only break in the flue above y119.
route.not_skippable: the flue is solid blackstone from the pad to y119 on all four faces; the parapet above the crown floor is three courses, which no player climbs from the gallery's level.

route.why: four sampling hoods, two by two, one at each corner of the crown floor, all four rimmed in cut copper so the rim tells you nothing. Three are dry: six down onto packed straw, with a ladder back up to the crown. The south-east one is the cooled throat - thirteen down, and the four lanterns in the basin put light and a water surface at the bottom of it. The clue is what is in the hole, not what is round it. The waypoint is (6171,120,4997), the crown floor west of the hood's rim: the hood's own cells are the hole and nobody stands in them.
route.not_skippable: the crown is sealed: parapet on four sides, the roof above, and a floor that is solid apart from the four hoods. There is no way off it but back down the gallery or into a hood.

route.why: thirteen blocks down the cooled throat into three courses of water. Water takes the whole of a fall of any height, so the leap costs nothing but nerve; a wrong hood costs six onto straw and a climb back.
route.not_skippable: this is the only way into the basin. The basin's four walls are the flue's footing, its ceiling is the basalt course at y110 and the throat is the one hole in it.

route.why: the basin's water surface is exactly the hall's floor level, so a player surfaces and walks east out of it: two blocks of passage cut through the flue's east wall and the vault's west wall at y107-108, threshold solid at y106 so the water stays in its box.
route.not_skippable: nothing gates it; it is the far side of the leap.

route.why: the assay vault: the spawner on a redstone block set into its floor with two air cells over it, his chest two east and two south, the core-reading benches along the walls. Copper grates in the vault's north and west walls show the drill floor and the east ambulatory, so a player who has not solved it has already seen him.
route.not_skippable: the vault has exactly three openings: the passage from the basin, the grates, which nothing passes, and the geyser, which only goes up. This is the only rctmod:trainer_spawner in the town once the shell is down.

route.why: the tapped geyser: soul sand at y103 under sixteen courses of water in a one-block shaft cased in blackstone, from three below the vault's floor to the gallery's level. The way to its foot is the sump in the vault's floor at (6178,4999) and the two-course adit north under the casing - the column cannot be entered at the vault's own level without draining it. The bubble column carries a player up and sets them down on the casing's head at y119, a step from the gallery.
route.not_skippable: not a route step: the way back, and the vault's only exit. A soul-sand bubble column cannot be swum down, so it is not a way in either - which is what makes the vault's one door the basin's, and it is why the exit is not a ladder: a ladder is two-way and would skip the hoods, the leap and the basin. THIS IS THE ONE MECHANIC THIS BUILDING DEPENDS ON AND IT HAS NOT BEEN SEEN RUNNING. If a bubble column can be descended, the vault is reachable without the leap; if it does not lift sixteen courses, a player who beats Blaine is shut in. Both are for the in-game check. There is no ladder fallback: a ladder would break the gate.

trainers_why: none authored here, and deliberately, as gym 1. A gym trainer has to be unavoidable, and unavoidability on this route is a claim about where a player can physically stand - the independent movement model (tools/gym_interiors_independent.py) is what settles it, and it is not this unit's to write (CLAUDE.md principle 16). The rejected interior's three researchers (Rim, Core, Vent) are a good handoff for whoever seats them: the drill floor, the gallery and the crown are the three places a walker cannot avoid.

no_build.why: the whole hall. Authored, not wired: the scene runtime's adventure-mode box (tools/scenes_pack.py no_build) needs a scene record in data/scenes.json and that is not written in this unit. Until it is, a player with blocks can bridge from the gallery to the crown's parapet or pillar out of the basin.

spawn_suppression.note: data/spawn_suppression.json gym_blaine, unchanged and not touched here. The whole of this building's bounds lies inside it (x6156..6182 inside 6152..6183; z4983..5007 inside 4976..5015), forecourt and eaves included, which is why the water in the basin and the geyser is not an exposure: no wild spawn is rolled in the box at all.

blocks_why: the town's own palette (docs/world-building/TOWN_CHARACTER.md gym7_town: blackstone, basalt, tuff, terracotta, acacia and copper instruments) minus terracotta, which is the houses' colour and not the works'. Water and soul sand are here for the basin and the geyser and for nothing else; both are boxed. No grass, no leaves, no carpet, and no magma block anywhere a player walks.

parts.why: gym 7, Blaine: the Assay House (data/gym_buildings/gym7.json). Run after the donor shell is taken down and the works under it filled in (tools/gym_demolish.py), which is after the pack donors are placed.

the tapped column inside it: sixteen courses of water in a one-block shaft, boxed by the casing on four sides from the vault's floor up and open only at the top. Its foot is three courses BELOW the vault's floor, at y104, because a sealed water column cannot be entered from a dry room: any opening cut in the casing puts air beside the water and the column drains into the vault (GYM_BUILDINGS_REVIEW.md D8 and its mutation test). The way in is the drowned adit below, which passes under the casing's own footing.

and the soul sand under it, at y103. The bubble column is the vault's only exit and it goes one way: a player is carried from the adit at y104 to the surface at y119 and steps west onto the casing's head, level with the gallery. It has to be one-way, because it is the only one-way lift vanilla has - a ladder or a stair out of the vault would also be a way in, and would skip the hoods, the leap and the basin. Not verified in a running game - route step 9 says what rides on it.

-- the geyser's sump, cut through the vault's own floor in its north-east bay: three courses of water whose surface is the floor, so a player walks into it and sinks. This is the mouth of the drowned adit to the column's foot. Sealed on all four sides by the vault's floor slab at y106 and by rock at y104-105.

the adit itself: two courses high so a player has head room, running north under the casing's footing at y106 from the sump to the column's foot. Two courses is the point - one course would put the player's head inside the slab above and no body position would be legal, which is why every attempt to open the casing at the vault's own floor level failed.
